deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is a prose draft of the methodological conclusion of Riemann's Inaugural Dissertation (1851), 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. It corresponds to §20, whose fair-copy version is on the next page ('§. 20. Die Einführung der complexen Größen ...').

The argument of the page, in order:
(1) The main purpose of the preceding investigations was to prepare, in general, a route already used successfully in particular cases. That route goes from the general concept of a function (its 'Gestalt', i.e. its value for every value of the argument, fixed by the conditions of the earlier sections) to its analytic expressions.
(2) For now he leaves aside the study of the expressions of a function. My reading of the image is 'schließen ... aus' ('exclude'), not 'schlugen ... ein'.
(3) He also leaves undiscussed the 'bridge' question between the two domains. This is the question whether the concept of a function of a complex variable used here (in modern terms, a holomorphic or meromorphic function on a domain or Riemann surface) coincides with that of a dependence expressible by 'Größenoperationen'. The next page's footnote lists these as the arithmetic operations together with differentiation and integration.
(4) He confines himself to applying his theorems to particular functions in the general case where the function of a complex variable depends on a many-valued function. This is the setting of functions on a branched, multi-sheeted covering surface T over the plane, i.e. a Riemann surface. For this a 'geometric garb' is appropriate.

The previous page supplies the concrete principle behind this programme: if T covers the whole plane, simply or multiply, and only poles of finite order are allowed, the function is algebraic. The present page frames that principle programmatically and contains no further derivation.
errors: No mathematical errors: the page contains no mathematical assertions to check. The 'bridge' question is explicitly left open rather than answered.

results.what: Methodological programme: characterize a complex function intrinsically (by its domain or covering surface, its singularities and its boundary conditions) and only afterwards derive its analytic expressions; leave open whether this concept coincides with functions given by finitely many operations.
results.modern_name: Intrinsic or conceptual definition of analytic functions (the Riemannian approach, as opposed to Weierstrass's power-series or expression-based approach); multivalued functions handled via Riemann surfaces

results.what: Restriction to functions depending on a many-valued function, treated in geometric form, i.e. on a multi-sheeted branched surface over the plane
results.modern_name: Riemann surfaces of multivalued (e.g. algebraic) functions
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1851 dissertation; developed further in Riemann 1857 (Abelian functions)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of a known passage of Riemann's published dissertation (§20), including its well-known remark leaving open whether the concept of a complex function coincides with expressibility by quantity operations. It contains no new mathematics; at most it documents the drafting stages of a published text.
transcription_corrections: Line 6: 'Wir schlugen jedoch [?] die Betrachtung der Ausdrücke einer Function gegenwärtig ein [?]' most likely reads 'Wir schließen jedoch die Betrachtung der Ausdrücke einer Function gegenwärtig aus'. 'Exclude' fits the following 'und lassen auch hier ... unerörtert'.
Line 8: 'welche den Mittelpunkt zwischen beiden Gebieten' more likely reads 'welche das Mittelglied zwischen beiden Gebieten (gleichsam die Brücke) bildet'.

The marginal addition 'Gestalt.' in line 2 seems to be an alternative or insertion relating to 'von ihrem (allgemeinen) Begriffe zu ihren Ausdrücken'. It matches the next page's use of 'Gestaltung der Function'.

Near the end: in 'wo die Function[-en-] einer veränderlichen {+complexen [?]+} Größe', 'Functionen' is struck and the insertion reads roughly 'einer veränderlichen'. The adjective before 'Function' could be 'mehrdeutigen' or 'vieldeutigen'; the reading is uncertain. 'abhängt [?]' is plausible.
